query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a controlled amount of Zr into the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy will overcome performance limitations by stabilizing a non-equilibrium solid solution and suppressing stable intermetallic formation, thus improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of a controlled amount of Zr
generation.conditions: Target density below 6 g/cm3, room temperature, and high-temperature environments
generation.structural_mediator: Stabilization of a non-equilibrium solid solution
generation.mechanism: Suppression of stable intermetallic formation through Zr addition
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.boundary: Composition: 1-5 at.% Zr, temperature: 20-500°C, exposure time: 1-100 hours, test environment: air and corrosive media
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Zr required for optimal performance and the potential effects of Zr on other properties, such as ductility and fracture toughness, are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with Zr-added and Zr-free Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, tested in room temperature and high-temperature environments
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Zr-added alloy does not exhibit improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation compared to the Zr-free alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
